title: Airworthiness Directives; General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (Type Certificate Previously Held by RUAG Aerospace Services GmbH) Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH (General Atomics) Model Dornier 228-100, Dornier 228-101, Dornier 228-200, Dornier 228-201, Dornier 228-202, and Dornier 228-212 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of specific part-numbered hydraulic pump motors becoming severely damaged by excessive heat. This AD requires replacing the affected hydraulic pump motor with an improved design hydraulic pump motor. This AD also prohibits installing an affected hydraulic pump motor on any airplane. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
summary: This matching program will support the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and the Department of War (DoW) in meeting the requirements set forth in Section 559(b) of the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, which requires the Secretary of Education and the Secretary of War to enter into a matching program to identify servicemembers and staff eligible for certain public service loan forgiveness programs. Under this matching program, DoW (source agency) will disclose to the ED, Federal Student Aid (FSA), (recipient agency), information on individuals who, at any time beginning on or after October 1, 2007, were members of the Armed Forces serving on active duty for a period of more than 30 consecutive days or civilian employees of DoW, for the purposes of: (1) identifying whether they made one or more student loan payments eligible to be counted for purposes of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program under subsection 455(m) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) and Temporary Expanded PSLF (TEPSLF) program; and (2) without requiring further information from them, certifying the total period of such service or employment for purposes of such program and counting the total number of qualifying payments made by them for purposes of such program during such period. ED will evaluate the information that it receives from DoW to create a count of qualifying payments under PSLF made by covered employees on their respective Title IV Loans (as defined herein). In addition, ED will create customized notifications for covered employees based on the status of their respective Title IV Loans and whether they have already submitted a PSLF and TEPSLF Certification and Application (PSLF form).

title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
summary: FinCEN is issuing this proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements under the Customer Due Diligence Rule consistent with the policy goals of, and as directed by, Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System. Specifically, the proposal ensures financial institutions covered by the Customer Due Diligence Rule collect sufficient information to verify the identities of beneficial owners of legal entity customers and maintain the authority, where warranted, to obtain additional information, including information relevant to whether the beneficial owners of legal entity customers possess lawful immigration status and employment authorization in the United States when such information is relevant to assessing risks.

summary: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval for a renewed information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following collection of information was published on July 20, 2026. FAA received five comments to this notice. The collection involves a request that airplane operators subject to the applicability of Annex 16, Volume IV of the Convention on Civil Aviation (hereinafter the "Chicago Convention") submit electronically an Emissions Monitoring Plan (EMP), an annual Emissions Report (ER), and an optional annual ER Eligible Fuels Annex (EFA) to the FAA. The information to be collected is necessary because FAA will use the information to fulfill the United States' responsibilities under the Chicago Convention.

title: Medicare Program; CY 2027 Part A Premiums for the Uninsured Aged and for Certain Disabled Individuals Who Have Exhausted Other Entitlement
summary: This notice announces Medicare's Hospital Insurance Program (Medicare Part A) premium for uninsured enrollees in calendar year (CY) 2027. This premium is paid by enrollees aged 65 and over who are not otherwise eligible for benefits under Medicare Part A (hereafter known as the "uninsured aged") and by certain individuals with disabilities who have exhausted other entitlement. The monthly Medicare Part A premium for the 12 months beginning January 1, 2027 for these individuals will be $597. The premium for certain other individuals as described in this notice will be $328.

title: Medicare Program; CY 2027 Inpatient Hospital Deductible and Hospital and Extended Care Services Coinsurance Amounts
summary: This notice announces the inpatient hospital deductible and the hospital and extended care services coinsurance amounts for services furnished in calendar year (CY) 2027 under Medicare's Hospital Insurance Program (Medicare Part A). The Medicare statute specifies the formulae used to determine these amounts. For CY 2027, the inpatient hospital deductible will be $1,776. The daily coinsurance amounts for CY 2027 will be as follows: $444 for the 61st through 90th day of hospitalization in a benefit period; $888 for lifetime reserve days; and $222 for the 21st through 100th day of extended care services in a skilled nursing facility in a benefit period.

title: Medicare Program; Medicare Part B Monthly Actuarial Rates, Premium Rates, and Annual Deductible Beginning January 1, 2027
summary: This notice announces the monthly actuarial rates for aged (age 65 and over) and disabled (under age 65) beneficiaries enrolled in Part B of the Medicare Supplementary Medical Insurance (SMI) program beginning January 1, 2027. In addition, this notice announces the monthly premium for aged and disabled beneficiaries, the deductible for 2027, and the income-related monthly adjustment amounts to be paid by beneficiaries with modified adjusted gross income above certain threshold amounts. The monthly actuarial rates for 2027 are $418.70 for aged enrollees and $452.40 for disabled enrollees. The standard monthly Part B premium rate for all enrollees for 2027 is $209.40, which is equal to 50 percent of the monthly actuarial rate for aged enrollees (or approximately 25 percent of the expected average total cost of Part B coverage for aged enrollees). The 2027 premium is 3.2 percent or $6.50 higher than the 2026 standard premium rate of $202.90. The Part B deductible for 2027 is $292.00 for all Part B beneficiaries. If a beneficiary has to pay an income-related monthly adjustment amount, that individual will have to pay a total monthly premium of about 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost of Part B coverage. Beginning in 2023, certain Medicare enrollees who are 36 months post kidney transplant, and therefore no longer eligible for full Medicare coverage, can elect to continue Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs by paying a premium. For 2027, the immunosuppressive drug premium is $125.70.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program

Under this matching program, DOL, as the source agency, will disclose Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA) payment data to SSA, the recipient agency. SSA will use the FECA payment data or the purpose of facilitating the administration of title II Disability Insurance (DI) benefits to eligible beneficiaries and their auxiliaries. title: Realty Action: Modified Competitive Sale of 20 Parcels of Public Land in Clark County, Nevada; Modification of Recreation and Public Purposes Act Classification
summary: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) proposes to offer 20 parcels of public land, totaling 200.64 acres in the Las Vegas Valley (Valley), by modified competitive sale at no less than each parcel's fair market value (FMV) pursuant to the Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act of 1998 (SNPLMA), as amended. The sale would be processed in conformance with applicable provisions of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (FLPMA) and BLM regulations. A 4.88- acre parcel proposed for inclusion in the sale was previously part of Recreation and Public Purposes (R&PP) Act lease N-75746. At the request of the lessee, the City of Las Vegas, the BLM approved the relinquishment of these acres from the lease. Because the parcel is no longer subject to the R&PP lease, the BLM proposes to modify the R&PP classification by removing the classification from the 4.88-acre portion of the parcel. This modification is necessary because lands that retain R&PP classification are not available for disposal under SNPLMA, and removing the classification makes parcel NVNV106381471 eligible for nomination in the 20-Parcel SNPLMA Land Sale.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-15-02, which applies to all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 900 airplanes. AD 2024-15-02 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-15- 02, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-15-02 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Air Plan Approval; Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) for Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) Control Technique Guidelines (CTG) Under the 2008 and 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving four State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania on May 10, 2023, January 20, 2026, February 17, 2026, and April 10, 2026, through the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (PADEP). The SIP revisions address reasonably available control technology (RACT) requirements for the 2008 and 2015 ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS) relating to control technique guidelines (CTGs) for volatile organic compounds (VOC) via previously adopted CTG regulations, three new CTG regulations and permits for four facilities covered by the CTG for the Manufacture of High-Density Polyethylene, Polypropylene, and Polystyrene Resins respectively. The EPA is approving these revisions to the Pennsylvania SIP in accordance with the requirements of the Clean Air Act (CAA).

title: Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-12-17, which applies to certain ATR--GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42-300, -320, and -500 airplanes; and all Model ATR72-101, -102, -201, -202, -211, -212, and -212A airplanes. AD 2021-12-17 requires a detailed visual inspection of each affected part for deficiencies (sealant blockage and out of tolerance ligaments), and depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-12-17, it was determined that additional seat track part numbers and airplanes may be affected. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2021-12-17 and would require inspections of additional parts. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Approval and Promulgation of State Air Quality Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Texas; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills
summary: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or the Act), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving the CAA section 111(d) State plan submitted by the State of Texas for sources subject to the Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Landfills Emission Guidelines (EG). The Texas MSW landfills plan was submitted to fulfill the State's obligations under CAA section 111(d) to implement and enforce the requirements under the MSW Landfills EG. The EPA is approving the State plan and amending the agency regulations in accordance with the requirements of the CAA.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-14-09, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X, FALCON 900EX, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. AD 2024-14-09 requires replacement of certain titanium screws, adds other locations for screw replacement, and revises the applicability from AD 2022-02-10. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-14-09, affected parts have been found in other areas of certain FALCON 7X airplanes as well as in additional FALCON 7X airplanes. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-14-09 and would require expanding the applicability to additional airplanes, expanding the locations for screw replacement, and revising the compliance times for parts replacement. This AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3 and EC635T2+ helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that the manufacturer's service material does not provide complete instructions for the inspections after a hard landing. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection of the tail rotor control system and, depending on the inspection results, corrective actions. This proposed AD would also require revision of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

These are revisions to the District's New Source Review (NSR) air permitting program rules for new and modified sources of air pollution under Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") section 110(a)(2)(C) and part D of title I.

title: Veteran Readiness and Employment Program: Update to Reduced Work Tolerance and Basic Eligibility Period
summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) proposes to amend the Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E) regulations to align with current practice and statute. The rule would expand the list of approved providers for reduced work tolerance (RWT) documentation, allowing for more accurate and timely processing by a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor (VRC). VA also proposes to clarify that a veteran who is subject to a basic period of eligibility would receive a new 12-year period of eligibility if such veteran obtains a compensable service-connected disability rating based on a subsequent period of active-duty service. Finally, the rule would remove the eligibility termination date for veterans discharged on or after January 1, 2013, consistent with the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020.
